dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: The data set covers all relevant process steps / technologies over the rail transport cargo system with a good overall data quality. The inventory is based on industry and literature data. The utilization ratio of the train is 40%. Mix of 86% electric trains and 14% diesel trains.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: The data set is representative for the mentioned region.The geographical representativeness concerning the related country as well as its DQR is related to relevance of the contributors. Possible geographical variance of minor contributors below the cut-off criteria are not affecting the geographical representativeness of the overall process, but are positively affecting the completeness of the model.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
This dataset contains the production phase of the train (capital goods) and the use phase of the train (including energy consumption) allocated to 1 tkm transported good. It also includes the construction of the railway track infrastructure used by the train (a piece of railway track allocated to 1 tkm transported by train). As default settings for the train parameters, a utilization ratio of 40% and a lifetime of 30 years were chosen. For railway track production, an average German railway track is accounted, see table. To know how much railway track infrastructure is needed for one freight train, the entire railway track infrastructure and the entire train fleet are considered. Allocation was applied by tkm and pkm (1 pkm= 0,1 tkm). Thus, one piece of railway track including it`s materials consumed (see table attached) is allocated to the train according to it`s tkm transported. Mix of 86% electric trains and 14% diesel trains.
Electric trains: Rail transport via electric cargo train driven by electricity. This transport dataset refers to 1 tkm and includes the electricity, train production and railway track infrastructure. The shares have been calculated by using the gross domestic product. End-of-life treatment of the train is not part of the data set. The background system is addressed as follows: Electricity, Thermal energy: The electricity (and thermal energy as by-product) used is modelled according to the individual country-specific situation. The country-specific modelling is achieved on multiple levels. Firstly the individual power plants in service are modelled according to the current national grid. This includes net losses and imported electricity. Second, the national emission and efficiency standards of the power plants are modelled. Third, the country-specific fuel supply (share of resources used, by import and / or domestic supply) including the country-specific properties (e.g. element and energy contents) are accounted for. Fourth, the import, transport, mining and exploration processes for the energy carrier supply chain are modelled according to the specific situation of each power-producing country. The different mining and exploration techniques (emissions and efficiencies) in the different exploration countries are accounted for according to current engineering knowledge and information. Diesel trains: Rail transport via diesel cargo train. This transport dataset refers to 1 tkm and includes the fuel, train production and railway track infrastructure. The shares have been calculated by using the gross domestic product. Variable parameters are: distance, ppm_sulfur, share_CO2_bio and utilisation. End-of-life treatment of the train is not included. Upstream processes for fuel production (e.g. exploration and production of fuels, refinery, transport) are included in the data set.
technology.technologicalApplicability: Rail transport of bulk commodities or packaged goods.

mathematicalRelations.modelDescription:
This aggregated dataset does not contain parameters. The user wishing to adjust the model to their individual circumstances may please refer to the 1st level disaggregated version of the data.
For mathematical model details concerning the implementation of the CCF formula see: http://www.gabi-software.com/fileadmin/GaBi_Databases/PEF_CFF_model_description.pdf

LCIMethodAndAllocation.deviationsFromLCIMethodApproaches:
Foreground system: no allocation is applied.
Background system: Within the refinery allocation by net calorific value and mass is used. For the combined crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids production allocation by net calorific value is applied.
LCIMethodAndAllocation.modellingConstants: Direct land use change: GHG emissions from direct LUC allocated to good/service for 20 years after the LUC occurs. Carbon storage and delayed emissions: credits associated with temporary (carbon) storage or delayed emissions are not considered in the calculation of the EF for the default impact categories. Emissions off-setting: not included Fossil and biogenic carbon emissions and removals: removals and emissions are modelled as follows: All GHG emissions from fossil fuels (including peat and limestone) are modelled consistently with the ILCD list of elementary flows. In the case that the emissions refer to the molecules CO2 and CH4, they are modelled as ‘carbon dioxide (fossil)’ and ‘methane (fossil)’. Biogenic uptake and emissions are modelled separately. For land use change, all carbon emissions and uptakes are inventoried separately for each of the elementary flows. Soil carbon accumulation (uptake) via improved agricultural management is excluded from the model.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataCutOffAndCompletenessPrinciples:
A cut-off rule based on mass or energy flow or the level of environmental significance of max. 3% is applied and confirmed by the reviewer. An active cut-off within the system has not been applied, no data gaps are known and all elementary flows of environmental effect are included in the inventory.
Capital goods (including infrastructures) and their end of life are included unless the exclusion is clearly documented and conform with the cut-off principles.
System boundaries include all known processes linked to the product supply chain.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.deviationsFromCutOffAndCompletenessPrinc: The train production (capitals goods) and railway track production (infrastructure) are included in this dataset. The End- of Life of train production and railway track production are excluded due to insignificance, therefore the secondary material input is also modelled burden free (cut-off), keeping consistency.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataSelectionAndCombinationPrinciples: LCI modeling is fully consistent. EF Energy datasets are consistently used.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataTreatmentAndExtrapolationsPrinciples: Several data sources have been averaged. Measured data from representative transport systems have been upscaled.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.useAdviceForDataSet:
Notice: this data set supersedes the EF3.0-compliant version (see link under "preceding data set version" below calculated with the EF3.0). The life cycle inventory is not changed from the original EF3.0 data set. The LCIA results are calculated based on the EF3.1 methods which provide updated characterisation factors in the following impact categories: Climate Change, Ecotoxicity freshwater, Photochemical Ozone Formation, Acidification, Human Toxicity non-cancer, and Human Toxicity cancer. The review report and the data quality ratings refer to the original results. The data set has been updated by the European Commission on the basis of the original EF3.0 data set delivered by the data provider.
Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) datasets to be used for implementing regular Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) studies and Organisation Environmental Footprint (OEF) studies exclusively under the specified Product groups and sectors as defined in the Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules (PEFCR) and Organisation Environmental Footprint Sectorial Rules (OEFSR) listed in https://ec.europa.eu/environment/eussd/smgp/ef_transition.htm The datasets are specifically designed for these methodological requirements (see above) and the related LCIA methods (listed below) recommended in EF.

review.common:reviewDetails: The dataset is compliant to "Zampori L., Pant R.: Suggestions for updating the Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) method, 2019 and Fazio S., Zampori L., De Schryver A. et al.: Guide for EF compliant data sets, Version 2.0, 2020. review.common:otherReviewDetails: Good overall quality (2,50) interpreted into "good quality" in the PEF quality validation scheme. The quality indicator for completeness was not requested to be quantified as a single DQI for all tenders. If a value “Not evaluated / unknown” completeness is given, this indicates that a single DQI was not explicitly requested but the completeness is still to be understood as very good. The Data Quality Indicator Results are conservative expert judgements, confirmed or - if necessary - corrected by the reviewers, based on their methodological as well as process understanding and considering semi-quantitatively the contribution of the DQIs of the used EF energy and transport datasets and of EF-related DQIs provided and reviewed within the GaBi databases. The overall DQIs of the datasets take into account primarily the quality and representativeness of the foreground technology information and that of the key upstream processes. If datasets are e.g. energy and transport intensive - or gain credits from energy recovery - the DQIs of the used EF energy and transport datasets influence the overall DQI significantly and have stronger been taken into account, via expert judgement. Analogous applies for other key background datasets. For the DQIs of the mentioned GaBi secondary datasets, similar DQIs had already been assigned to those datasets and were considered by the reviewers via expert judgement when assigning of the overall DQIs. In case of doubt, lower (i.e. lower quality) DQIs were assigned.
